name: Shudder to Think
label: Dischord
lede: Shudder to Think ran a glam falsetto through Dischord's straight-edge corridors, took a Buzz Clip to Sony, scored films for a decade, and came back to Dischord twenty-seven years later with a new single.

eras.title: From Stüge to Shudder to Think
eras.text: They started as teenage hardcore and found a singer who preferred falsetto to barking. Dischord calls them part of a younger wave, inspired by the scene but independent of it.

years.h: Stuart Hill and Mike Russell start a hardcore band called Stüge
years.p: Hill plays bass and Russell drums, with guitarist Sam Fleming and singer Bobby Jones. The name isn't Shudder to Think yet.

years.h: A school play gives Stüge its singer
years.p: Fleming and Jones leave for college. Hill recruits guitarist [[Chris Matthews|824d9e26-0d6b-4ec7-b7af-78505ed771b0]] from the new wave band 3-2-1, and Matthews points to [[Craig Wedren|2da87294-e651-420b-8d25-2dbc3b29a285]], whom he'd watched in a school play.

years.h: Russell names the band on the way to practice
years.p: He says he shudders to think they'd end up just another hardcore band. The phrase sticks, and the music starts drifting toward post-hardcore.

years.h: Curses, Spells, Voodoo, Mooses on Sammich, not Dischord
years.p: The debut album comes from a small label. Dischord's catalog lists it among the releases it distributes.

eras.title: Glam in a straight-edge town
eras.text: The odd band on a label known for fury: melodic, theatrical, a little strange. By 1992 half the band had changed, with Nathan Larson arriving from Swiz and Adam Wade from Jawbox.

years.h: Ten Spot is Dischord No. 46
years.p: The band had already turned up on Dischord's State of the Union compilation. Now it gets its own record, sung in falsetto on a label known for barking.

years.h: Funeral at the Movies follows as No. 54
years.p: It's later bundled with Ten Spot as a single release, No. 55.

years.h: Matthews plays his last show; Nathan Larson takes the guitar
years.p: Matthews leaves for school. [[Nathan Larson|c0845dd8-ef14-486c-92b6-260727732b4c]], who had played bass in [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]], moves to guitar.
years.xp: Within six months drummer Mike Russell left too, leaving Craig Wedren and Stuart Hill as the only members from the 1980s records.

years.h: A show in Albig, Germany becomes a live record
years.p: The date on the band's German tour is released as Your Choice Live Series Vol. 21 on Tobby Holzinger's Your Choice label.

years.h: Mike Russell plays his last show, and a Jawbox drummer steps in
years.p: Russell, behind the kit since the Stüge days, is replaced by [[Adam Wade|d2502278-bf42-445b-98a2-9249af4c8a0a]], just out of [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]].

years.h: Get Your Goat is the last album before Epic
years.p: Dischord No. 67, the final full-length before the band leaves for a major label.

eras.title: Buzz Bin, of all places
eras.text: Tours with Fugazi and The Smashing Pumpkins put the band in front of far bigger crowds, and Epic signed them. By Dischord's count, only one other band ever left the label for a major.

years.h: A tour with Fugazi, then another with the Smashing Pumpkins
years.p: The first is with the D.C. flagship, the second with a Chicago band on its way to arenas.

years.big: "We wanted our music to reach the most people and make a living."
years.h: Shudder to Think sign with Epic and move to New York
years.p: Craig Wedren on why the band left Dischord. A&R man Michael Goldstone championed them at Epic. [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]] was the only other Dischord band to make the jump.
years.xp:
Dischord's own band page says Shudder to Think became one of only two bands to leave the label for a major. Looking back, the band has described Epic as supportive throughout.

Not every fan agreed. Wedren told PopMatters that "a fan picket[ed] our show" while they were opening for [[The Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]], on Dischord's behalf.

years.h: Pony Express Record, tracked to analog tape in a big room
years.p: [[Ted Niceley|fbe203ef-a327-4d7e-af16-a10d55b7347d]], who had also worked with Fugazi and Girls Against Boys, produces for what the band called a widescreen sound.
years.xp:
The drums were locked to a click the band nicknamed the Russian Dragon. Adam Wade explained it: "Are you rushin' or are you draggin'?" He called it "brutal, but this record could not be as great as it is without that."

Per Wikipedia, the album had sold 30,000 copies in the U.S. by late October 1994, and 60,000 by February 1997.

q: I worshipped them. There was one year I saw them twelve times.
years.h: X-French Tee Shirt lands in MTV's Buzz Bin
years.p: The single also reaches No. 36 on the Radio & Records alternative chart.
years.xp:
PopMatters dates the Buzz Bin run to spring 1995. Rolling Stone cited it as "the video that signaled the end of the Buzz Bin."

The song outlived the argument. [[Deftones|7527f6c2-d762-4b88-b5e2-9244f1e34c46]] have covered it live, and [[Incubus|e3e0abcd-7671-4482-a9d8-462f5acc9be5]] played part of it at Lollapalooza 2003.

years.h: Craig Wedren is diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma at 26
years.p: It comes shortly after promotion for Pony Express Record begins, he told Vanyaland in 2025. His doctor told him, "We know how to cure this."
years.xp:
Wedren has said he didn't fear dying at the time. Wikipedia says he beat the cancer over the next few years.

The band kept going, but its next album, 50,000 B.C., didn't land, and by 1998 the energy had moved to film scores.

years.h: Jeff Buckley and James Iha both go public as fans
years.p: In a 1995 interview, [[Jeff Buckley|e6e879c0-3d56-4f12-b3c5-3ce459661a8e]] counts Shudder to Think among the bands he loves, and [[James Iha|a89811cc-4514-48b2-b353-dba9debf7055]] of the Smashing Pumpkins calls them a wholly original rock band.
years.xp: The same year Epic released So Into You as a single.

eras.title: One flop, three films, no band
eras.text: 50,000 B.C. missed, and the band's energy moved toward film. By 1998 they had music in three movies and an invitation from Pearl Jam. Then Nathan Larson left.

years.h: Kevin March of the Dambuilders takes over the drums
years.p: [[Kevin March|5f5f1eb3-c441-4758-b5a0-8873f098735e]], drummer of [[The Dambuilders|baf6c035-1e22-4a4c-ad4b-ea294fd41a1b]], replaces Adam Wade.

years.h: 50,000 B.C. is the second and last Epic album
years.p: Reviews are mixed, and Wikipedia calls it a commercial flop.

years.h: Two films scored, two songs in a third
years.p: The band scores High Art and First Love, Last Rites and places two songs in Todd Haynes's glam-rock film Velvet Goldmine. It's the road Wedren and Larson follow for decades.
years.xp:
High Art came out on Velvel and First Love, Last Rites on Epic's soundtrack arm. The Velvet Goldmine songs sat alongside the film's glam covers and originals.

After the band stopped, film work became both men's day job. Wedren went on to score Wet Hot American Summer, School of Rock and Yellowjackets; Larson scored films and played in his band Hot One.

years.h: Pearl Jam take Shudder to Think to Australia
years.p: Pearl Jam invite the band on their Australian tour and work a snippet of the Shudder song Pebbles into their own set.

years.h: Nathan Larson leaves, and the band stops
years.p: Craig Wedren goes on to score Wet Hot American Summer, School of Rock and later Yellowjackets. Larson scores films for Todd Solondz and Lilya 4-ever.

eras.title: Two coasts, two drummers
eras.text: The reunion was loose by design: a hired guitarist and bassist, and a different drummer depending on the coast. It ended with a 2009 farewell at the Bowery Ballroom, then came back once more for the Black Cat's 20th birthday in 2013.

years.cap: Nathan Larson and Craig Wedren, Mercury Lounge, New York, September 17, 2007
years.h: First show in nearly a decade, at the Mercury Lounge
years.p: Craig Wedren, Nathan Larson and Kevin March play with Mark Watrous on guitar and Jesse Krakow of Time of Orchids on bass.

years.cap: Craig Wedren with Kevin March on drums and Mark Watrous on guitar, New York, September 2007
years.h: Kevin March drums the East Coast, Adam Wade the West
years.p: The reunion keeps rolling with two drummers. March covers the eastern dates; Wade comes back for the western ones, New Orleans included.

years.h: Reunion show at the 9:30 Club, October 10, 2008
yt: Reunion show at the 9:30 Club, October 10, 2008

years.h: Live from Home documents the reunion shows
years.p: A live album on Team Love.

years.cap: Craig Wedren at the Bowery Ballroom, New York, March 2007
years.h: Goodbye at the Bowery Ballroom, with Chris Matthews for the encore
years.p: Shudder to Think play a farewell show in New York. Founding guitarist [[Chris Matthews|824d9e26-0d6b-4ec7-b7af-78505ed771b0]] joins them for the last song.

years.h: The Pony Express Record line-up plays the Black Cat's 20th birthday
years.p: Craig Wedren, Nathan Larson, Adam Wade and Stuart Hill play the D.C. club's anniversary, with Chris Matthews and Mike Russell joining for the encore.

eras.title: Twenty-seven years, and Dischord again
eras.text: Craig Wedren survived a heart attack in 2018. Seven years later came what the reunions never offered: new songs, beginning with Thirst Walk and Playback, on the label the band once left for a major.

years.src: Vanyaland · The Chronicles of Michael Christopher
years.h: Craig Wedren has a heart attack at 48
years.p: Paramedics carried him out on a stretcher at 2 a.m. while his son watched, he has said. Years of panic attacks followed.
years.xp: He told Vanyaland the heart attack left him depressed and anxious, waking between 2 and 4 a.m. afraid of dying. It also gave him, in his words, "such a will to live."

yt: Hit Liquor, Permanent Records Roadhouse, March 15, 2025
years.h: Two surprise shows in Los Angeles, and a new song
years.p: Craig Wedren, Nathan Larson and Adam Wade, with Clint Walsh on guitar and [[Jherek Bischoff|e0dcef88-0353-425c-99bd-81a36e96ed7f]] on bass, play Permanent Records Roadhouse and debut Playback.
years.xp: Vanyaland reports the band announced its first tour in 17 years. Wedren said he'd send voicemail ideas every year or two, and then, as he put it, "it's just stars aligned."

years.h: Back on Dischord at No. 201, with Thirst Walk
years.p: Thirst Walk backed with Playback is the band's first new music since the late 1990s. Dischord takes preorders on its site and Bandcamp.
years.xp: Stereogum's headline counted 27 years since the last new music. The band that left Dischord for Epic in the 1990s is back on the label.

years.h: Who Sent You? arrives the night of the Philadelphia show
years.p: Three new songs, released digitally. New York follows September 12 and Los Angeles September 20, with the Thirst Walk 7" repressed for the merch table.
